purpose: Advisory vocabulary for translating animation and visual-development craft into observable production facts.

terms.purpose: Place a beat at a precise time and give it a readable duration.
terms.use_when: A change, reaction, impact or pause must land on a known beat.
terms.expansion: State the start and end time, what changes at the accent, and what remains held afterward.

terms.purpose: Control how far a subject travels between successive poses.
terms.use_when: The same action must feel slow, fast, accelerating or decelerating.
terms.expansion: Describe the early, middle and late travel distances and the resulting speed curve in screen space.

terms.purpose: Give every frame a new drawing or state for maximum continuity and fluidity.
terms.use_when: A delicate continuous motion or fast camera path needs no intentional exposure hold.
terms.expansion: State that the specified motion updates every frame and name the feature that must remain readable.

terms.purpose: Hold each drawing for two frames to retain hand-drawn cadence while preserving readable motion.
terms.use_when: A 24 fps anime-like action needs controlled stepped rhythm.
terms.expansion: Name the held pose, the two-frame exposure, and the exact accent where the next drawing replaces it.

terms.purpose: Hold a drawing for three frames for a deliberate broad or economical beat.
terms.use_when: A stylized pause, heavy gesture or broad transition benefits from a stronger stepped cadence.
terms.expansion: State which pose is exposed for three frames and how the next change avoids a frozen performance.

terms.purpose: Preserve a pose or composition long enough for the audience to read it.
terms.use_when: A reaction, eye line, impact result or final state needs visual proof.
terms.expansion: Give the hold interval, the unchanged anchors, the breathing or eye activity allowed during it, and the release trigger.

terms.purpose: Make one beat dominate a sequence of smaller actions.
terms.use_when: A line, glance, impact or gesture needs a clear editorial or acting emphasis.
terms.expansion: Identify the preceding preparation, the accented action, its sound, and the recovery after the accent.

terms.purpose: Create a rapid change of pose, direction or gaze with minimal transitional travel.
terms.use_when: A comic reveal, sharp look or decisive attack needs immediate clarity.
terms.expansion: Describe the before pose, the short transition window, the new silhouette and the exact visual cue that makes the snap readable.

terms.purpose: Temporarily reduce vertical travel or motion change so a jump or impact reads in the air.
terms.use_when: A leap, recoil or comic suspension needs a readable apex.
terms.expansion: State the apex interval, the body orientation, the force that produced it and the event that starts descent.

terms.purpose: Shape acceleration and deceleration around a movement.
terms.use_when: A camera move, hand reach, turn or settle should feel weighted rather than linear.
terms.expansion: State where acceleration begins, where maximum speed occurs, where braking begins and which body part leads.

terms.purpose: Use separated short beats with visible stops or releases.
terms.use_when: A comic, nervous or percussive performance needs discrete beats.
terms.expansion: List each short beat, its stop or release, the sound cue and the next trigger; do not call the whole sequence merely staccato.

terms.purpose: Maintain an unbroken flowing transition between actions.
terms.use_when: A graceful camera path, gesture or emotional turn must avoid visible resets.
terms.expansion: Describe the overlap between successive actions and the continuous path of the body or camera.

terms.purpose: Define a decisive pose that carries story or physical information.
terms.use_when: A beat needs a pose that can be checked independently.
terms.expansion: Describe the silhouette, weight distribution, facing, hands, gaze and the fact this pose proves.

terms.purpose: Mark the furthest stretch, compression or directional limit in a motion.
terms.use_when: An action needs a readable maximum before reversing or settling.
terms.expansion: Name the body parts at maximum extension or compression and the force that returns them.

terms.purpose: Specify the transitional drawing that explains how two key poses connect.
terms.use_when: A transition risks teleportation, limb merging or an unclear axis.
terms.expansion: Describe the passing body line, support point, limb path and the exact continuity it preserves.

terms.purpose: Fill the visible path between designed poses without changing the intended action.
terms.use_when: A generated motion must preserve a specific route between anchors.
terms.expansion: State what interpolates, what remains fixed, and which feature is checked for continuity.

terms.purpose: Mark the neutral or crossing position through which a body moves.
terms.use_when: A turn, walk, reach or swing needs a clear midpoint.
terms.expansion: Give the midpoint time, support leg or pivot, facing and the direction of travel.

terms.purpose: Plan a controlled sequence from approved extremes and keys.
terms.use_when: A staged acting beat or complex shot needs deterministic anchors.
terms.expansion: List the approved key poses in order and describe the transition rule between each pair.

terms.purpose: Let a continuously changing action evolve forward without pre-locked keys.
terms.use_when: Fluid effects, chaotic debris or a naturally unfolding gesture benefits from organic change.
terms.expansion: Define the start constraint, the allowed evolving variables and the invariant that must never drift.

terms.purpose: Keep the whole body organized around a readable directional curve.
terms.use_when: A pose must communicate force, attitude or travel direction instantly.
terms.expansion: Describe the curve from head through torso to support or extremity and how it changes across the beat.

terms.purpose: Capture the whole-body intent before small anatomy details.
terms.use_when: A fast action or expressive pose risks becoming stiff or over-described.
terms.expansion: State the dominant action line, weight shift, asymmetry and emotional read in visible body behavior.

terms.purpose: Make pose, prop and character separation readable in outline.
terms.use_when: Characters overlap, backlight or move quickly.
terms.expansion: State the negative gaps, limb separation, prop outline and screen contrast that must remain visible.

terms.purpose: Keep body, costume or prop volume stable through perspective and deformation.
terms.use_when: A turning body, stretch, squash or foreshortened limb risks morphing.
terms.expansion: Name the volume anchors and the allowed deformation while preserving identity landmarks.

terms.purpose: Prepare the audience for an imminent action through a visible counter-movement or attention shift.
terms.use_when: A jump, strike, turn, line or reveal needs causal setup.
terms.expansion: State the preparatory movement, target of attention, duration and the trigger that releases the main action.

terms.purpose: Let a moving part pass its final mark before returning to a controlled settle.
terms.use_when: Hair, cloth, hands, head or camera should show inertia.
terms.expansion: Name the final target, the amount and direction of overshoot, and the returning settle.

terms.purpose: Show the body absorbing motion and arriving at a stable state.
terms.use_when: A gesture, impact, landing or line should end with a believable tail.
terms.expansion: Describe decaying movement, breath, eye activity, weight distribution and the held final state.

terms.purpose: Continue secondary parts after the main body action has changed direction.
terms.use_when: Hair, tail, coat, props or hands need to preserve momentum.
terms.expansion: State the primary stop or reversal, the delayed secondary movement and its stop condition.

terms.purpose: Let adjacent actions overlap so performance does not read as isolated commands.
terms.use_when: Speech, gaze, hand gesture, breath or camera motion should blend.
terms.expansion: Name the outgoing beat, incoming beat, overlap interval and which anchor remains readable.

terms.purpose: Delay a part behind the leading body or prop to show inertia or resistance.
terms.use_when: Cloth, hair, tail, sleeves or a heavy object should lag behind movement.
terms.expansion: Specify the leader, lagging part, delay and material response before it catches up.

terms.purpose: Add a subordinate behavior that supports the primary intention without stealing focus.
terms.use_when: A character must feel alive during a main action or line.
terms.expansion: State the primary action, the secondary behavior, its timing and why it remains subordinate.

terms.purpose: Use the head or eyes to initiate a turn before the torso follows.
terms.use_when: A look, suspicion, discovery or conversational turn needs readable attention.
terms.expansion: State the eye lead, head rotation, torso follow and the final eyeline target.

terms.purpose: Make attention travel visibly from one target to another.
terms.use_when: Dialogue, reveals and reactions depend on where the character looks.
terms.expansion: Name the starting target, path, pause, ending target and the facial or body change caused by the look.

terms.purpose: Use inhale, suspension and exhale to expose thought and physical effort.
terms.use_when: A line, fear response, exertion or quiet reaction needs an embodied rhythm.
terms.expansion: State the breath phase, chest/shoulder motion, vocal effect and the beat it prepares or releases.

terms.purpose: Place an intentional blink as a readable micro-reaction.
terms.use_when: A character masks surprise, resets focus or punctuates a line.
terms.expansion: Give the blink time, trigger, eyelid duration and the changed gaze or expression after it.

terms.purpose: Bind visible mouth shapes to the original spoken words and syllable rhythm.
terms.use_when: Any intelligible dialogue is present.
terms.expansion: State the language, exact source words, syllable-aligned mouth movement, pause, emphasis and voice priority over noise.

terms.purpose: Show the exact bodies, limbs, surfaces and direction at contact.
terms.use_when: A strike, collision, grab or block must be physically legible.
terms.expansion: State attacker, target, contact point, support point, facing, direction and the state immediately after contact.

terms.purpose: Show the target or weapon moving away after force is received.
terms.use_when: An impact must have a visible consequence.
terms.expansion: State the force source, travel direction, body compression, displacement and recovery path.

terms.purpose: Isolate the instant of decisive contact with readable shape and contrast.
terms.use_when: A hit or collision needs a sharp visual accent.
terms.expansion: Give the frame or time window, contact geometry, silhouette, flash or camera response and the next state.

terms.purpose: Represent a very fast transition as a designed elongated or blurred drawing.
terms.use_when: A hand, weapon, head or body crosses too quickly for ordinary in-between detail.
terms.expansion: Name the moving mass, direction, stretch shape, duration and the anchor that remains readable.

terms.purpose: Temporarily elongate a body or prop along travel direction to communicate speed.
terms.use_when: A stylized fast action needs acceleration without losing the character identity.
terms.expansion: State the axis of stretch, preserved identity landmarks, release point and return to volume.

terms.purpose: Keep a limb, body or camera on a continuous geometric path.
terms.use_when: An attack, dodge, throw or tracking move risks arbitrary direction changes.
terms.expansion: Describe the origin, apex, endpoint, radius or curvature and the force or intention driving the arc.

terms.purpose: Show where force enters, travels through a body or prop and exits as motion.
terms.use_when: A strike, push, fall or throw must avoid weightless motion.
terms.expansion: Name source, contact, resistance, body chain, transferred direction and visible result.

terms.purpose: Show the opposing mass, friction or bracing that shapes an action.
terms.use_when: A block, shove, grapple or heavy object must feel grounded.
terms.expansion: State the resisting surface or body, support points, compression and the moment resistance yields or holds.

terms.purpose: Convert an incoming line into a new trajectory through a block, catch or body turn.
terms.use_when: A missed or blocked attack should causally create the next action.
terms.expansion: State incoming line, redirecting contact, pivot, outgoing line and the defender's resulting orientation.

terms.purpose: Make the intended path and target of an attack explicit.
terms.use_when: Multiple limbs or characters risk ambiguous targeting.
terms.expansion: State the attacker, target point, screen direction, body alignment and whether the line is blocked, dodged or lands.

terms.purpose: Prevent an exchange from silently flipping screen direction.
terms.use_when: A chase, duel or multi-cut fight depends on consistent left/right geography.
terms.expansion: State the screen axis, each subject's side, facing and the permitted crossing event.

terms.purpose: Use a cut during a continuous action so momentum carries across views.
terms.use_when: A new angle should intensify or clarify an action without resetting it.
terms.expansion: State the action phase at the cut, the carried velocity, the new camera target and the matching continuation pose.

terms.purpose: Arrange subjects, props and camera so the intended event reads at a glance.
terms.use_when: Blocking or emphasis is unclear.
terms.expansion: State foreground/midground/background placement, attention hierarchy, screen direction and the event the composition proves.

terms.purpose: Reserve readable empty area for gaze, motion, threat or reveal.
terms.use_when: A frame needs tension, direction or a clear landing zone.
terms.expansion: State where the empty area is, what it anticipates and which subject or movement must not fill it prematurely.

terms.purpose: Maintain consistent left/right or toward/away geography across cuts.
terms.use_when: A chase, dialogue exchange or fight depends on spatial continuity.
terms.expansion: State each subject's screen side, travel vector and any motivated axis crossing.

terms.purpose: Connect a subject's gaze to a specific target in space.
terms.use_when: Dialogue, reaction and off-screen threats need spatial proof.
terms.expansion: State eye height, target position, gaze direction and the camera side that preserves the relationship.

terms.purpose: Reveal footwork, ground contact and forward drive from a low moving camera.
terms.use_when: Running, pursuit or grounded combat depends on lower-body readability.
terms.expansion: State camera height, travel path, lens relation, subject feet and the ground landmarks that pass frame.

terms.purpose: Expose changing angles, spatial layout or converging paths from above.
terms.use_when: The audience must understand a multi-subject relationship.
terms.expansion: State the camera's overhead position, rotation or descent, the geometry revealed and the next readable action.

terms.purpose: Use a foreground obstruction to hide then reveal a subject or event.
terms.use_when: A reveal needs motivated occlusion rather than an arbitrary cut.
terms.expansion: Name the occluder, hidden subject, camera movement, reveal time and continuity anchors after reveal.

terms.purpose: Rapidly change framing to follow a decisive event or advantage.
terms.use_when: A sudden impact, gag or threat changes visual priority.
terms.expansion: State the trigger, new frame boundaries, pan/tilt or snap speed and the subject that inherits focus.

terms.purpose: Let audio continue over a change of picture.
terms.use_when: Dialogue, breath or ambience should bridge a cut.
terms.expansion: Mark the outgoing and incoming shot, the exact spoken source, the `<scenetrans>` boundary and the audio continuity rule.

terms.purpose: Introduce incoming audio before the new picture appears.
terms.use_when: A voice, impact or environment should motivate the next shot before the cut.
terms.expansion: State the audio entry time, source, picture cut time and the visual event it anticipates.

terms.purpose: Connect shots through matching shape, motion, gaze or action.
terms.use_when: A transition needs a visible reason and continuity cue.
terms.expansion: Name the matching feature in both shots and state the state that remains continuous across the cut.

terms.purpose: Temporarily freeze or nearly freeze an image to make a graphic beat readable.
terms.use_when: A titleless comic punch, impact flash or final pose needs a controlled hold.
terms.expansion: State the exact hold interval, permitted micro-motion, sound continuation and release condition.

terms.purpose: Separate depth layers and assign events to readable planes.
terms.use_when: Occlusion, scale or parallax matters.
terms.expansion: Place each subject or landmark in a named depth layer and state what can occlude or reveal what.

terms.purpose: Create controlled depth by moving or composing several spatial planes.
terms.use_when: A camera move needs depth without losing layout anchors.
terms.expansion: Name the planes, their relative motion or parallax and the fixed world landmark that prevents drift.

terms.purpose: Show depth through different apparent speeds of near and far elements.
terms.use_when: Tracking or lateral movement should communicate space.
terms.expansion: State near/mid/far travel rates, camera direction and the depth relation being proven.

terms.purpose: Use overlap, scale, focus, value or perspective to establish distance.
terms.use_when: A scene or giant subject risks reading flat.
terms.expansion: Name the cue, its screen location and how it changes during the shot.

terms.purpose: Preserve which body or object is in front of which at every beat.
terms.use_when: Characters interact closely or a reveal depends on a foreground layer.
terms.expansion: State the occluding edge, hidden contact, reveal condition and the identity landmark that remains visible.

terms.purpose: Introduce the stable geography before detailed action begins.
terms.use_when: A sequence or cut needs a reliable spatial baseline.
terms.expansion: Name entrances, exits, landmarks, subject positions and the screen direction that later shots inherit.

terms.purpose: Use a longer lens or aligned depth to make distant elements appear closer.
terms.use_when: A chase corridor, crowd or giant scale needs a controlled spatial read.
terms.expansion: State the lens relation, aligned depth elements and the motion cue that remains readable despite compression.

terms.purpose: Anchor architectural lines and movement directions in perspective.
terms.use_when: A corridor, street, platform or machine layout must stay geometrically stable.
terms.expansion: State the dominant vanishing point, lines that converge to it and the subject path relative to it.

terms.purpose: Retain a hand-drawn line character with selective broken contours.
terms.use_when: A loose anime or rough key-animation line quality is requested.
terms.expansion: State where contour breaks occur, which identity edges remain closed and how the line affects readability.

terms.purpose: Use line thickness to separate foreground, focal edges and recessive detail.
terms.use_when: Flat linework needs depth and attention control.
terms.expansion: Assign heavier and lighter edges to named planes or subjects and state the focal priority.

terms.purpose: Use visible brush variation inside shapes without losing color grouping.
terms.use_when: A hand-painted or sakuga-like fill is desired.
terms.expansion: State the brush direction or texture zones and the value boundary that must remain clean.

terms.purpose: Keep shadows in deliberate graphic shapes rather than smooth gradients.
terms.use_when: A 2D anime or graphic look must remain stable.
terms.expansion: Name key light direction, shadow planes, contact shadow and the transitions that remain hard-edged.

terms.purpose: Organize the image into readable light, middle and dark masses.
terms.use_when: Complex costumes, effects or dark scenes risk merging.
terms.expansion: Assign value groups to subject, environment and effect, and state the separation edge that must survive motion.

terms.purpose: Plan color progression across story beats or shots.
terms.use_when: Mood, time or narrative escalation is carried by palette changes.
terms.expansion: State the palette at the start, transition trigger, destination palette and the continuity colors that remain fixed.

terms.purpose: Separate a subject from a similar-value background with a motivated edge light.
terms.use_when: Dark costume, silhouette or scale needs readable separation.
terms.expansion: State the source direction, affected contour, color/value and where the rim light is deliberately absent.

terms.purpose: Reduce contrast and saturation with distance to reinforce depth.
terms.use_when: Large environments or layered backgrounds need scale and air.
terms.expansion: State how contrast, hue and edge sharpness change from foreground to distance.

terms.purpose: Make a high-speed path legible through directional graphic marks.
terms.use_when: A fast body, weapon or camera move needs visual support.
terms.expansion: State origin, direction, length, density, timing and the object whose motion the strokes prove.

terms.purpose: Use hair or flexible strands to reveal head movement and inertia.
terms.use_when: A character turn, impact or acceleration needs a secondary motion cue.
terms.expansion: State the head lead, hair delay, arc direction and settle point without changing hairstyle identity.

terms.purpose: Show the path and scale of particles released by a physical event.
terms.use_when: Breakage, impact or giant movement needs environmental proof.
terms.expansion: Name source surface, launch direction, particle size groups, gravity response and landing region.

terms.purpose: Stage dust as a time-bound release, expansion and decay rather than permanent fog.
terms.use_when: A landing, skid or impact produces localized dust.
terms.expansion: State source contact, burst onset, expansion boundary, transparency decay and what remains visible through it.

terms.purpose: Use a brief graphic flash to punctuate contact without replacing the physical event.
terms.use_when: A hit or collision needs a readable accent.
terms.expansion: State trigger contact, flash duration, shape/color, screen region and the underlying body reaction that remains visible.

terms.purpose: Organize an effect into causal phases.
terms.use_when: Energy, fluid, debris or light must have a complete lifecycle.
terms.expansion: Give four consecutive time windows and the visible state, sound and lighting change in each phase.

terms.purpose: Separate effect materials so density, silhouette and light contribution stay legible.
terms.use_when: A complex effect combines fragments, smoke and light.
terms.expansion: For each channel state presence, shape, motion, depth and interaction with the environment; give a reason when absent.

terms.purpose: Ensure every requested technique becomes a concrete production field.
terms.use_when: A prompt contains many trigger words or specialist modules.
terms.expansion: For each selected term record its field, observable fact, camera or sound evidence and acceptance check.

terms.purpose: Keep an identity, prop, landmark or state stable across a cut.
terms.use_when: A segment or multi-segment sequence must join cleanly.
terms.expansion: Name the anchor, its before state, after state, screen position and the evidence that proves it persisted.

terms.purpose: Verify that an action or design can be identified at the intended speed and scale.
terms.use_when: A fast cut, dark scene, overlap or effect risks visual ambiguity.
terms.expansion: State the event to identify, viewing condition, minimum visible cue and failure correction.

terms.purpose: Verify positions, facing, depth and screen direction across time.
terms.use_when: Characters, camera and environment interact across multiple shots.
terms.expansion: List the spatial facts to compare at shot boundaries and the allowed transformation between them.

terms.purpose: Bind a sound, spoken syllable or musical accent to its visible cause.
terms.use_when: Dialogue, impacts, footsteps or L/J cuts are important.
terms.expansion: State source, time window, visible cause, voice priority and the continuity rule across cuts.

terms.purpose: Record the exact state that a shot hands to the next shot.
terms.use_when: A motion, expression, prop or effect continues across a cut or segment.
terms.expansion: State body pose, gaze, prop ownership, velocity, sound tail and camera relationship at the final held moment.
